docs.title: BRIDGE Measurements: design notes
docs.text: BER hackathon, 2026-09-30. Companion to bridge_measurements.yaml (validated with linkml lint / gen-pydantic; example instances in examples/ validate with linkml validate).

docs.title: The problem
docs.text:
The harmonization-targets matrix shows three incompatible ways BER schemas say "we measured X on Y and got Z":

Pattern Who Property identity Value Weakness for a union Slot-per-property NMDC (166 MIxS QuantityValue slots, 139 TextValue slots on Biosample) the slot name / slot_uri (MIxS CURIE) inlined AttributeValue objects (has_numeric_value, has_unit) new property = schema change; property is not queryable as data Column-per-analyte BASALT (~30 wide *Product tables) the column name (total_carbon_id, sand_pct_id, respiration_co2_c_ug_per_g) mixed: QuantityValue refs, bare doubles with units in the column name no property vocabulary at all, no unit field for many columns Row-per-observation (OGC O&M) BASIN-3D (MeasurementTimeseriesTVPObservation) data: observed_property → a 166-term synthesis vocabulary TimeValuePair series + unit_of_measurement vocabulary is basin3d-local; single (non-series) measurement class never materialized

The harmonization row for Measurement/observation itself says it: "No shared slot names across families — harmonize against O&M/SOSA semantics rather than slot spellings."

docs.title: The union model
docs.text:
Only the row-per-observation shape can host the other two. A slot-per-property record trivially unpivots into rows (one per populated MIxS slot); a wide product table unpivots into rows (one per analyte column); an O&M observation already is a row. The reverse projections are impossible without schema-per-source. So the BRIDGE Measurement class is O&M/SOSA-shaped:

Measurement
  observed_property  → ObservedProperty (BERVO-first vocabulary)   "what"
  feature_of_interest + type + position                            "of what"
  result             → polymorphic MeasurementValue                "the value"
  phenomenon_time / result_time                                    "when"
  statistic / aggregation_duration / replicate_role                "as summarized how"
  quality_status / quality_flags                                   "how trustworthy"
  method / instrument / was_generated_by / part_of_collection      "how produced"
  datasource + *_source_* slots                                    "round-trip provenance"

Every source-facing controlled slot has a verbatim-source companion (observed_property_source_term, source_quality_label, raw_value) so the union is lossless: you can always recover what the source actually said. This is BASIN-3D's MappedAttribute lesson (keep source and synthesis terms side by side), flattened into paired slots plus an external SourceTermMapping crosswalk table instead of a nested object per slot — friendlier to Parquet/ lakehouse layouts.

docs.title: Precedents deliberately reused
docs.text:
• NMDC PropertyAssertion is NMDC's own property-as-data class (used only by misc_param, aligned with BERtron's properties pattern). Measurement is declared close_mappings: nmdc:PropertyAssertion, and its slots carry exact_mappings to nmdc:has_attribute_id, nmdc:has_numeric_value, etc.
  • BASIN-3D enums are adopted nearly verbatim: StatisticEnum, ResultQualityStatusEnum (with basin3d's documented synonym sets in the descriptions), SamplingMediumEnum, AggregationDurationEnum, TimeReferencePositionEnum, and the TimeValuePair result.
  • BASALT QC and replicate semantics: QualityFlagEnum is ProcessedDataFlag + plate-well flags; replicate_role/replicate_number/ summary_of capture Single/Replicate/Average including the average→members link BASALT keeps as _avg columns; feature_position captures core_section and well position; MeasurementCollection is the product/run (shared method, instrument, activity, data file, summary_metrics).
  • Two-level quality on purpose: coarse quality_status (validated/unvalidated/suspect/rejected/estimated — the search facet) and fine quality_flags (below-detection, outlier, blank... — the analytics detail). Sources populate one, the other, or both.

docs.title: Enumerations vs permissible values vs subclassing
docs.text:
The rule proposed here: closed enums for process/QC dimensions, an open vocabulary class for the observed property, and subclasses only for result structure.

  1. Closed enums (statistic, quality, medium, aggregation, replicate role): small, stable, cross-domain value spaces. Source codes map in via SourceTermMapping; each enum keeps an OTHER/NOT_APPLICABLE escape.
  2. Open vocabulary for observed_property: thousands of properties, growing per campaign — an enum would relive NMDC's 166-slot problem inside an enum. Instead ObservedProperty is a first-class descriptor (id, label, categories, measurement_of, measured_in, canonical_unit, value_type) that is exactly the shape of a BERVO Variable term (bervo:BERVO_measurement_of, measured_in, has_unit, has_value_type pre-coordinations). BERVO term exists → use its CURIE; BERVO term missing → mint a descriptor with the same slots and treat it as a BERVO candidate. BERVO adoption becomes an id swap, not a remodel.
  3. Subclassing: only structural — TimeSeriesMeasurement pins result: TimeSeriesValue. Domain subclasses ("RespirationMeasurement", "PHMeasurement"…) are discouraged: BASALT's 30 product classes and NMDC's 166 slots are both cautionary tales of encoding the property in the schema. If a portal wants typed views (as geochem-demo's RadonObservation does), define them as profiles/views that constrain observed_property, not as the storage model.
  4. Value polymorphism replaces the has_*/plain naming schism (harmonization row 17, "strongest centralization target"): MeasurementValue → QuantityValue | ControlledTermValue | TextValue | BooleanValue | TimestampValue | TimeSeriesValue, plain slot names (numeric_value, unit) with exact_mappings to the NMDC has_* family, NMDC's type-designator convention for polymorphic documents, and raw_value everywhere. Units: UCUM strings now; seed a future shared UnitEnum from NMDC's 109-code UCUM enum.

docs.title: Projection recipes
docs.text:
• NMDC: for each populated measurement slot on Biosample → one Measurement: observed_property_source_term = the slot's slot_uri, observed_property via the crosswalk, feature_of_interest = biosample id, result copied field-for-field (has_numeric_value→numeric_value…). ControlledTermValue slots (env_medium…) land as term results. NMDC's flattener (nmdc-lakehouse-schema) already emits per-slot columns; the same transform targets rows instead.
  • BASALT: each *Product row → one MeasurementCollection + one Measurement per analyte column. Column name → observed_property_source_term; unit comes from the linked QuantityValue.has_unit or is parsed from the column-name suffix (_ug_per_g, _mg_per_kg) — recorded in SourceTermMapping.unit once, not re-parsed per row. flag_<analyte> → quality_flags; measure_type/replicate → replicate_role/ replicate_number; <x>_avg columns become AVERAGE rows with summary_of pointing at the replicate rows. WellReading → a Measurement with feature_position = well, its parent PlateProduct = the collection.
  • BASIN-3D / USGS / AmeriFlux: MeasurementTimeseriesTVPObservation → TimeSeriesMeasurement almost 1:1; a compound mapping row (USGS 00010 → water-temperature + WATER) fills observed_property and sampling_medium from one source code, exactly as basin3d's :-compound mappings do.

docs.title: Open questions for the group
docs.text:
1. BERVO scope: BERVO today is EcoSIM-simulation-variable heavy. Do we grow BERVO to cover lab analytes (total C, ions, enzymes) and phenotyping traits, or federate (BERVO + MIxS + TO/PATO) under ObservedProperty.mappings?
  2. Naming family: this draft uses plain value-slot names with mappings to NMDC has_*. If NMDC/BASALT ingest friction matters more than lambda/BERtron/CDM alignment, flip it — the crosswalk is symmetric.
  3. Identity/granularity: is a Measurement row id-worthy ({datasource}:{record}:{term} deterministic ids proposed), and do we materialize replicate-level rows or only averages for the search index?
  4. Feature of interest: this module keeps feature_of_interest as a loose uriorcurie + type enum. It should eventually range over the central BRIDGE FeatureOfInterest role class (harmonization row 3), which is its own hackathon-sized design.
  5. Timeseries storage: inline TimeValuePair lists work for exchange, but lakehouse storage likely wants the points in a long table keyed by measurement id — same schema, different physical layout.
  6. Where it lives: drop this module into bridge-central-schema (ber_central_schema.yaml is currently a template stub) as its first real content?

docs.title: BRIDGE Central Schema
docs.text:
The central BRIDGE schema for harmonized cross-BER data access. This root schema defines the shared base elements and composes domain modules; each module corresponds to one or more rows of the BER harmonization-targets matrix (see the lakehouse-registry repo).

Modules: - measurements.yaml: the unified Measurement / ObservedProperty model (harmonization rows: Measurement/observation, Observed property, QuantityValue). Designed at the 2026-09-30 BER hackathon against NMDC, BASALT, and BASIN-3D as reference schemas, with BERVO as the primary observed-property vocabulary.

Planned modules (not yet designed): - feature-of-interest (Sample / Site / ObservationTarget role class) - agents (Person / Organization / Contribution) - datasets (Dataset / DataObject / Study)

docs.title: ber-central-schema
docs.text:
The central BRIDGE schema for harmonized cross-BER data access. This root schema defines the shared base elements and composes domain modules; each module corresponds to one or more rows of the BER harmonization-targets matrix (see the lakehouse-registry repo).

Modules: - measurements.yaml: the unified Measurement / ObservedProperty model (harmonization rows: Measurement/observation, Observed property, QuantityValue). Designed at the 2026-09-30 BER hackathon against NMDC, BASALT, and BASIN-3D as reference schemas, with BERVO as the primary observed-property vocabulary.

Planned modules (not yet designed): - feature-of-interest (Sample / Site / ObservationTarget role class) - agents (Person / Organization / Contribution) - datasets (Dataset / DataObject / Study)

URI: https://w3id.org/ber-data/bridge-central-schema

docs.title: Slot: canonical_unit
docs.text: Preferred reporting unit as a UCUM code, e.g. "mg/L", "Cel", "umol/L".

docs.title: Slot: categories
docs.text: Classification path in priority order (BASIN-3D style), e.g. ["Biogeochemistry", "Anions"]. Use BERVO upper-level variable branches (e.g. "Soil biogeochemistry variable") when possible.

docs.title: Slot: data_object
docs.text: Pointer(s) to the source data file(s) (checksum+size+format+URL core, harmonization row 7).

docs.title: Slot: description
docs.text: A human-readable description for a thing

docs.title: Slot: feature_of_interest
docs.text: Id of the entity the property was measured on: an NMDC biosample (nmdc:bsm-...), a BASALT ProcessedSample, a BASIN-3D MonitoringFeature, a plate well's parent culture, an organism. Kept as a loose pointer so this module doesn't import every sample/site class; the central BRIDGE FeatureOfInterest role class (harmonization row 3) is the eventual range.

docs.title: Slot: feature_position
docs.text: Sub-feature locator when the feature is measured at a position: plate well ("A01"), core section ("TOP"/"MID"/"BTM"), depth interval, timepoint label.

docs.title: Slot: id
docs.text: Unique id. For lakehouse-materialized measurement rows a UUID or source-derived deterministic id (e.g. "{datasource}:{source_record}:{source_term}").

docs.title: Slot: label
docs.text: Human-readable name, e.g. "Nitrate", "Soil respiration".

docs.title: Slot: mappings
docs.text: Cross-vocabulary equivalents, e.g. MIXS:0000425, USGS parameter codes as CURIEs.

docs.title: Slot: measured_in
docs.text: The medium/compartment the property is characteristically measured in (e.g. ENVO or BERVO context term). Mirrors bervo:BERVO_measured_in.

docs.title: Slot: measurement_of
docs.text: The entity or quality quantified, e.g. a CHEBI analyte or PATO quality. Mirrors bervo:BERVO_measurement_of.

docs.title: Slot: name
docs.text: A human-readable name for a thing

docs.title: Slot: numeric_value
docs.text: The value; for ranges, use minimum/maximum instead or additionally (midpoint).

docs.title: Slot: observed_property_source_term
docs.text: The verbatim source-native property code (NMDC slot name / MIxS CURIE, BASALT column name, USGS parameter code), preserved for round-tripping. Resolved to observed_property via SourceTermMapping.

docs.title: Slot: part_of_collection
docs.text: The assay run / product / dataset this measurement belongs to.

docs.title: Slot: phenomenon_time
docs.text: ISO-8601 instant or interval when the property applied to the feature (collection/observation time, not lab-analysis time).

docs.title: Slot: point_quality
docs.text: Per-point quality, as in BASIN-3D ResultListTVP.result_quality.

docs.title: Slot: quality_flags
docs.text: Fine-grained QC flags (BASALT ProcessedDataFlag family); per-measurement, not per-run.

docs.title: Slot: raw_value
docs.text: The value exactly as it appeared at the source ("65 umol/L", "2-4 cm", "Fair"), preserved verbatim for provenance and re-parsing.

docs.title: Slot: replicate_role
docs.text: BASALT measure_type - whether this is a single reading, one replicate, or the average.

docs.title: Slot: result
docs.text: Polymorphic result; type designator on the value picks the subclass.

docs.title: Slot: result_time
docs.text: ISO-8601 time the result was produced (e.g. lab analysis date).

docs.title: Slot: source_quality_label
docs.text: Verbatim source QC code (USGS "A"/"P", BASALT flag, well flag), for round-tripping.

docs.title: Slot: source_term
docs.text: The source's native code exactly as it appears in the data: a USGS parameter code ("00010"), an NMDC slot_uri (MIXS:0000425), a BASALT column name ("total_carbon"), a FLUXNET variable ("FC").

docs.title: Slot: source_term_description
docs.text: The source's own description of the term.

docs.title: Slot: source_vocabulary
docs.text: The vocabulary this term originates from, e.g. "BERVO", "MIxS", "USGS-PCode", "BASALT-column".

docs.title: Slot: summary_metrics
docs.text: Run-level summary key-values (BASALT summary_metrics; plate blank_mean, cv_percent).

docs.title: Slot: summary_of
docs.text: For AVERAGE (or other summary) rows - the member replicate measurements.

docs.title: Slot: term_id
docs.text: e.g. a PATO, ENVO, or CHEBI CURIE.

docs.title: Slot: time_reference_position
docs.text: Whether timestamps mark the START, MIDDLE, or END of each aggregation interval.

docs.title: Slot: type
docs.text: Class designator (NMDC convention) so polymorphic rows/documents resolve to their class.

docs.title: Slot: value_type
docs.text: Whether values are quantitative or qualitative. Mirrors bervo:BERVO_has_value_type.
